title: The development loop, uninterrupted.
text: EDIT → COMPILE → CONTINUE The development loop, uninterrupted. Your application takes time to start. Your next edit shouldn’t have to. Reclazz brings supported Java and Spring changes into the running JVM. Keep your development session moving, with a clear account of what changed and what still needs a restart. Get your first reload ↗ Check a change → ● ● ● your development session // Change the behavior public String message() { return "Ready for the next idea." ; } EDIT → COMPILE → LIVE Same JVM. Updated behavior. title: More than replacing bytecode
text: More than replacing bytecode 01 Observe compiled output Your build writes class files into watched directories. Automatic source compilation is an optional route. 02 Apply a supported change The agent uses JVM redefinition and, on stock JDKs, a companion engine for supported structural edits. 03 Refresh framework state Spring integrations update supported bean, mapping, listener and metadata paths. Check the runtime result. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Know exactly what “reload” means
text: Know exactly what “reload” means A successful class replacement, a recreated bean and an updated database mapping are different outcomes. The guides keep those distinctions visible so you can choose the right edit and recovery path. Reloads Supported within its stated scope Conditional Requires a particular mode or shape Restart This edit needs a restart Unverified Acceptance evidence is missing No reload No Reclazz change is applied State is specific to the path Method-body redefinition keeps existing object fields. A Spring singleton refresh destroys and recreates that bean and can reset its mutable state. Saving the previous code does not restore destroyed resources. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A source snapshot, with visible boundaries
text: A source snapshot, with visible boundaries This build documents source version 1.5.0 . Recorded capability evidence is pinned to 75535bd , scope reviewed on 19 October 2026 . Features on this source baseline may be absent from an older downloaded release. Match the agent and integrations, and confirm your installed version. Recorded tests cover named framework graphs, mostly stock SapMachine 17/21 on macOS arm64. “Java 17+” is a target requirement, not evidence for every JVM, operating system or framework combination. This documentation change does not rerun the agent’s acceptance suite. Explore versions, evidence and contribution →

title: Your first reload
text: Before you start The agent and MCP server target Java 17+ . JDK 17/21 are the baseline test lanes; the client matrix records narrower OS/framework coverage. This is not a guarantee for every later JDK or framework version. The IDE plugin declares IntelliJ builds 233 through 262.* (2023.3–2026.2). IDE compatibility and application-JVM compatibility are separate. SAP Commerce is needed only for the SAP route; see its guide . Stock JDKs support Reclazz's documented structural reload paths; a special JBR installation is not required to begin. Supported changes and native type limits are in usage and superclass feasibility . Examples use source version 1.5.0 . A source version is not proof that every registry has published it. Choose a version present in your chosen channel or build from source . Match the agent and its integration artifacts; newer BUILD/VERIFY/MCP features may require local builds. title: Gradle: add the plugin, keep your Boot setup
text: Gradle: add the plugin, keep your Boot setup For an existing Spring Boot application, retain its Spring Boot version and add the Reclazz plugin to its build.gradle.kts : kotlin plugins { id("com.onurkat.reclazz") version "1.5.0" } repositories { mavenCentral() } Start with ./gradlew bootRun (Windows: gradlew.bat bootRun ). In another terminal, compile edits with ./gradlew classes . The plugin attaches to bootRun and test JVMs. Plain application.run is opt-in with reclazz { applyToRun.set(true) } in a plugin build containing the new option; see the application run guide for its availability and scope. Automatic watching includes all main class outputs; an explicit watchDirs list replaces them in the Gradle options . If that plugin version is not available in the Plugin Portal, use a released matching version or the standalone route. A local agent can be selected via reclazz { agentJar.set(file("/absolute/path/to/agent-1.5.0.jar")) } ; this replaces agent resolution, not Gradle plugin resolution. Full setup: Gradle plugin . Read the complete reference →

title: Maven: use an opt-in development profile
text: Maven: use an opt-in development profile For an existing Spring Boot Maven project, merge these properties and profile into your POM; keep its existing Boot parent/plugin and dependencies. Put your other JVM arguments in app.jvmArgs rather than discarding them. The example marker is optional for your app, but proves preservation in the runnable demo. Do not predefine reclazz.agentArgs : prepare-agent supplies it before Boot's run goal is configured. xml <properties> <reclazz.version>1.5.0</reclazz.version> <app.jvmArgs>-Ddemo.marker=kept</app.jvmArgs> </properties> xml <profiles> <profile> <id>reclazz-dev</id> <build> <plugins> <plugin> <groupId>com.onurkat.reclazz</groupId> <artifactId>reclazz-maven-plugin</artifactId> <version>${reclazz.version}</version> <configuration> <propertyName>reclazz.agentArgs</propertyName> <platform>spring</platform> </configuration> </plugin> <plugin> <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId> <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId> <configuration> <jvmArguments>${reclazz.agentArgs} ${app.jvmArgs}</jvmArguments> </configuration> </plugin> </plugins> </build> </profile> </profiles> Start from the application directory: sh mvn -Preclazz-dev reclazz:prepare-agent spring-boot:run The explicit reclazz:prepare-agent goal supplies reclazz.agentArgs before Boot's run goal; watchDirs defaults to ${project.build.outputDirectory} . Do not omit that first goal: setting the property only inside Boot's forked initialize lifecycle did not propagate it to run in the tested Maven/Boot combination. The profile has no lifecycle execution, so the agent is prepared once. Boot consumes that property plus app.jvmArgs in its application JVM. The profile is inactive without -Preclazz-dev , and it does not add Reclazz to the packaged application. Existing Surefire/Jacoco argLine wiring is untouched; this profile is deliberately for the development app, not test-JVM attachment. Do not also add a manual Reclazz -javaagent to app.jvmArgs or a second prepare-agent execution. In another terminal, edit a method body and run mvn compile ; then check the running behavior without restarting. Wait for the watcher's default 30-second startup delay before the first edit. The complete runnable example shows the response and JVM-identity check. Plain compilation is not the optional whole-build safety wrapper . Read the complete reference →

title: IntelliJ IDEA: enable it for the project
text: IntelliJ IDEA: enable it for the project Open Settings → Plugins → Marketplace , search for Reclazz , install it and restart the IDE if prompted. Alternatively, use Install Plugin from Disk… with a plugin ZIP from GitHub Releases . Choose a release that actually contains the ZIP; the agent JAR is not the IDE plugin. Open the project and enable Settings → Tools → Reclazz → Enable Reclazz . It is off by default. This also works for non-SAP projects. Start a Java run configuration handled by the IDE. Reclazz supplies its bundled agent and watches the IDE's module compiler outputs. For a run delegated to Gradle or Maven, follow the Gradle or Maven setup rather than assuming IDE injection. Compile a small edit with the build that writes those watched outputs, then check the running application's response. Detailed options: usage . The ZIP contains agent/reclazz-agent.jar under the plugin's installed root; that bundled name is deliberately unversioned. No separate agent download is needed for IDE-managed runs. SAP launches outside the IDE use a staged copy; follow the SAP guide rather than persisting a path inside an IDE installation. For IDE-managed launches, one existing Reclazz VM option is reused only when its jar path and options exactly match what the IDE would inject, after quote parsing. A different path/version/options or multiple Reclazz flags stop launch with a conflict message. Remove the manual Reclazz VM option to use IDE settings, or disable Reclazz under Settings → Tools → Reclazz to manage attachment yourself. Other Java agents are preserved. Recognition covers reclazz-agent.jar and reclazz-agent-<version>.jar (version starts with a digit, classifiers allowed). Renamed jars at other paths, environment-provided flags and @argfiles are not inspected; option order and equivalent filesystem paths are not normalized.

title: Optional command-line plugin installation
text: Optional command-line plugin installation JetBrains documents installPlugins for its launchers. These examples use the 2026.2 launcher documentation , not a fresh OS/IDE installation test. Adjust the IDE path/name to your installation; older IDE launchers need their own check. sh # macOS, standalone IntelliJ IDEA installation open -na "IntelliJ IDEA.app" --args installPlugins com.onurkat.reclazz # Linux, example installation directory /opt/idea/bin/idea.sh installPlugins com.onurkat.reclazz bat :: Windows cmd.exe, with the IDE bin directory on PATH idea64.exe installPlugins com.onurkat.reclazz For Toolbox-managed IDEs, use the launcher name configured in Toolbox. These commands install the plugin only; still enable it for the project and start the application with the agent. See JetBrains' plugin installation and OS-specific launchers . Read the complete reference →

title: Standalone: attach at JVM startup
text: Standalone: attach at JVM startup Download reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar from the assets of your chosen GitHub release , or build from source . Replace X.Y.Z and the application paths. Keep the entire agent argument quoted when paths contain spaces. sh # macOS/Linux: compiled classes must be on this application's classpath java "-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=watchDirs=/absolute/app/target/classes" -cp "/absolute/app/target/classes" com.example.Main powershell # Windows PowerShell: adapt the main class and output directory java "-javaagent:C:/Tools/Reclazz/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=watchDirs=C:/Projects/app/target/classes" -cp "C:/Projects/app/target/classes" com.example.Main Add your normal dependency classpath/JVM options as needed; Windows classpath entries use ; instead of : . For an executable application JAR retain your normal -jar app.jar launch, while pointing watchDirs to the actual recompiled class output. Watching source files or merely rebuilding a JAR is not this recipe. The flag must be present at startup so classes are instrumented when loaded. The watcher defaults to a 30-second startup delay ; wait before your first edit. For a small standalone demo only, startupDelaySec=0 removes that wait. Agent arguments and framework-specific limits: usage . Read the complete reference →

title: 2. Observe a change in the same JVM
text: 2. Observe a change in the same JVM Start the application with the agent and confirm the target JVM is the one you intended. Connection alone only confirms connectivity. After the watcher starts, call an endpoint or method and record its response. Change a simple method's returned text, compile to a watched class output, then call it again without restarting . Expect the new text and the same JVM. For complete acceptance with matching agent/MCP builds, follow the Maven installation verification recipe from its baseline step before editing: confirm the intended JVM/version with DOCTOR, hash the compiled class, require a same-session applied VERIFY receipt, and check the changed response in the same JVM. A successful connection or compile alone never completes this check. If only connection succeeds, do not call installation accepted: check the agent was present at startup, the compiled output is watched, and the current change is supported. Troubleshooting . Validation scope for this guide: the Maven example and standalone launch were exercised on macOS arm64 with SapMachine 21; details are in the example . Windows/Linux commands, Marketplace installation, IDE launcher installation and a live SAP Commerce setup were not rerun for this change. Their references and existing coverage are separate from this local verification. Read the complete reference →

title: Edit an existing method body
text: Compile a supported edit into a watched output. Existing object fields remain on the JVM method-body-only path. Framework follow-up can separately recreate beans. Compile, check the same JVM and inspect the changed result.

title: Add or remove a method
text: Stock-JDK companion mode supports hot-compiled calls; new methods do not become native members of the original Class. A caller that still uses a removed method gets NoSuchMethodError, or the inherited implementation for a removed override, as after a restart. Compile affected watched callers; use a supported framework adapter for reflection.

title: Add an instance field
text: Stock mode stores added fields separately. Isolated initializers run on first read for existing objects; constructor-dependent or entangled initializers retain type defaults with a reason. Read the initializer diagnostic and verify an existing object.

title: Read/write an added field from another class
text: Both owner and caller must be watched/reloaded in the measured direct-access shape. Field-type changes and every inherited/loader variant are not certified. Compile both sides and check the shared value on an existing object.

title: Add a static field with an initializer
text: Compile-time constants and separable initializers, including bounded forward conditionals/switches, are supported. Existing static blocks and values are not reset. Check the new value and any extraction refusal reason.

title: Change an already initialized static field initializer
text: Later saves preserve the current added static value, including null or application writes. Reload does not replay arbitrary static initialization. Restart to run startup initialization again; account for external side effects.

title: Change an inlined compile-time constant
text: Callers can retain their old literal until recompiled. AutoCompile can rebuild detected watched sources; unwatched consumers remain outside that repair. Recompile affected callers or use supported AutoCompile.

title: Append an enum constant / remove its final constant
text: Documented on JDK 17–25 with ordinal-preserving edits. Existing application arrays sized from the old enum length do not grow. Check enum consumers and any fixed-size application arrays.

title: Insert/reorder enum values or remove a non-tail value
text: The edit renumbers ordinals; Reclazz refuses it. Restart alone does not migrate persisted ordinal data. Review persisted ordinals and restart for the type change.

title: Add or remove an implemented interface
text: Requires a compatible enhanced-redefinition JVM such as JBR/DCEVM. Stock JVMs refuse the type change. Use a supported enhanced runtime or restart.

title: Change a superclass
text: The loaded superclass stays unchanged. Eligible bodies may apply; dependent methods stay pinned and unsafe signatures/constructors can refuse the whole save. Read partial/refused reporting and restart for the hierarchy.

title: Discover added members through arbitrary reflection
text: On stock JVMs the original Class lacks companion members. Explicit framework adapters have separate scope; arbitrary reflective consumers do not. Restart, or use a compatible enhanced JVM/explicitly supported adapter.

title: Assume every Java 17+ vendor/version is certified
text: Java 17+ is the target. The main recorded portable lanes are stock SapMachine 17/21 on macOS arm64, not every vendor, OS or future JDK. Validate the exact runtime and change shape.

title: Refresh an affected singleton bean
text: Supported bean paths destroy/recreate the singleton and repair bounded references. Mutable bean state can reset; arbitrary external holders are not repaired. Check lifecycle effects, current references and the served result.

title: Add a new component class
text: Direct/composed stereotypes, native name/condition selection and singleton/prototype/lazy creation are supported. Not a repeat of full startup scanning. Compile the new class and check registration/condition outcome.

title: Add a component with a web/custom scope or scoped proxy
text: The new-component path refuses these scope shapes. Normal singleton/prototype support does not imply custom scope enrollment. Restart under the application’s normal configuration.

title: Reevaluate every filtered component after a profile/property edit
text: New-component conditions are registration-time decisions. General later rediscovery and startup import/auto-configuration replay are outside this path. Use a restart for a changed startup topology; validate any narrower path.

title: Add an @Bean factory method
text: Bounded lite/full/static configuration paths support documented arguments, aliases, selection and direct conditions. Existing names/custom scopes/unknown composed conditions are restricted. Use the exact factory allowlist and check product identity/lifecycle.

title: Change existing injection or lifecycle metadata
text: Spring metadata caches are refreshed on supported bean paths. Recreation has state and reference limits; it is not an arbitrary graph rewrite. Check the recreated bean’s injection and lifecycle behavior.

title: Add @PostConstruct / @PreDestroy methods
text: Supported plain singletons use the javax Spring 5 / Jakarta Spring 6 lanes. Each instance keeps its added destroy callback through later edits/removal. Verify creation/injection/destruction for the affected instance.

title: Add @Transactional or cache-advised service methods
text: Supported public singleton operations use native interceptors; bounded composed metadata is supported. Compile the caller and respect the proxy/advice allowlist. Verify commit/rollback or cache behavior, not only the method result.

title: Add pre/post authorization to a new service operation
text: Named classic/modern Spring Security graphs support direct and bounded composed policies. Unknown security infrastructure/advice shapes are refused. Check both allowed and denied calls with the installed security graph.

title: Edit an @Aspect pointcut
text: Updates supported existing mutable singleton JDK/CGLIB proxy chains. Previously unproxied targets and unsupported proxy shapes are outside this path. Check an already-injected reference and inspect unsupported targets.

title: Add/edit/remove @Scheduled methods
text: Direct no-argument void callbacks on supported singletons, with documented proxy/transaction/cache/async combinations. Removal cancels the registration. Check one current schedule and retirement of its predecessor.

title: Add/edit/remove @EventListener methods
text: Direct callbacks with one reference event input and void/single-event return on supported singletons. Filtering/order/conditions and advice have bounded scope. Publish a test event; check current delivery and no stale registration.

title: Add @TransactionalEventListener methods
text: Direct void methods on supported unproxied singletons; Spring handles phase/fallback/conditions/order. Reload retires queued callbacks from the old added registration. Check the intended transaction phase and a later edit/removal.

title: Add @Async service methods
text: Direct public methods support void, Future and CompletableFuture with native executor/error handling and supported transaction/cache advice. Check execution, returned completion and exception handling.

title: Reload a helper captured by a constructor-injected leaf
text: Exact supported factories, plain two-node shapes and one measured direct-child context form. Aliases, broader graphs, proxies/factory products and lifecycle-owned shapes are excluded. Read the ownership contract and verify the retained caller’s value.

title: Add/change a controller endpoint
text: Supported controller mapping rescans include added methods on stock JVMs. Receiver, metadata and classloader shapes still matter. Compile and send a request to the intended route.

title: Add @ExceptionHandler methods
text: Plain controllers/advice and standard resolver on Framework 5.3.39/6.1.14; bounded synchronous metadata. Proxy/inheritance/generic/composed/custom resolver shapes are excluded. Check status/body and handler precedence; fix ambiguous mappings.

title: Add @InitBinder / @ModelAttribute methods
text: Supported plain controller/advice adapters preserve named binding, model rules and native advice order/selectors. Read the exact callback allowlist. Check a real binding/model request through the current controller.

title: Add Jackson getters, setters or DTO fields
text: Supported Spring-managed mapper adapter; mutable DTOs and saved annotations. Final added fields are not writable; creator/record/builder additions are excluded. Check JSON input and output against the installed Jackson version.

title: Assume every serializer discovers companion members
text: Jackson’s explicit adapter does not establish arbitrary Gson/custom mapper or record-creator support. Stock original-class reflection remains limited. Validate the serializer or restart for native reflective visibility.

title: Change validation constraints on an existing field
text: Supported Hibernate Validator metadata caches are cleared in both javax/Jakarta factory discovery paths. Do not infer arbitrary validator/provider compatibility. Submit both invalid and valid input; inspect the native validation result.

title: Edit an existing Spring Security HTTP rule
text: Supported SecurityFilterChain beans rebuild into the live FilterChainProxy. Inline ignoring chains remain; a failed rebuild can keep the previous rules serving. Verify allowed and denied requests; inspect whether the new rules became live.

title: Add/edit/remove a Kafka listener
text: Plain singleton, direct callback, explicit literal ID, documented topic/group/options and standard record-mode factory. Native consumers retire before replacement. Verify message delivery, new route and old-consumer retirement.

title: Add/edit/remove a JMS listener
text: Plain singleton with standard processor/registry/default container factory. Literal or placeholder destinations/selectors; bounded result and callback shapes. Verify delivery/selector behavior and complete consumer destruction.

title: Add synchronous JMS replies
text: Documented return types and direct @SendTo. JMSReplyTo takes priority; null sends nothing. No arbitrary DTO/Future/reactive return claim. Check conversion, correlation and destination on a test request.

title: Add/edit/remove a Rabbit listener
text: Plain receiver, standard simple container, AUTO acknowledgment/default executor and bounded queue/options. Startup worker hook must track complete retirement. Wait for worker retirement and verify real message delivery.

title: Change a Kafka/Rabbit expression-driven route
text: Documented native SpEL values are reevaluated when the listener is saved. Evaluation occurs after old consumers retire and can fail without restoring them. Save the listener again and check the exact route/group.

title: Reroute consumers by changing only a routing property/bean
text: The documented added Kafka/Rabbit expression path does not automatically reroute on a property/bean-only edit; a listener re-save is the supported live action. Re-save/compile the listener, or restart for native startup resolution.

title: Recreate JMS/Kafka consumers after a helper/property save
text: Separately measured narrow root-context leaf-owner transactions; exact factories, constructor and callback shapes. Not arbitrary consumer graphs. Use the constructor ownership guide and check current-value delivery.

title: Recreate Rabbit consumers through property/dependency cascades
text: Measured on Framework 5.3.39/AMQP 2.4.17 and Framework 6.1.14/AMQP 3.1.7, stock JDK 17/21 on macOS arm64: one root context, plain local helper/leaf owner, one void literal-ID callback, native simple containers, AUTO acknowledgment and nontransacted channels. Verify current helper/owner values and complete worker retirement; unsupported ownership, stop timeout or partial reconstruction requires restart.

title: Reload one bean mixing Kafka/JMS/Rabbit consumers
text: Unsupported mixed ownership is refused before owned consumers retire. Single-broker coordination is not a combined broker transaction. Separate the ownership shape or restart.

title: Assume XA, hosted clusters, rebalances or exactly-once reload
text: Local broker observations do not certify every hosted/failure/transactional topology. Rabbit reply/async and broader custom container paths are separate gaps. Run targeted acceptance for your broker, lifecycle and delivery policy.

title: Edit recognized Boot properties
text: Candidate binding/conversion/validation occurs before live mutation. Uncheckable/invalid candidates remain pending; live setter/recreation failure can partially apply. Fix rejected input, save again and inspect actual runtime values.

title: Edit nested YAML values or indexed lists
text: Already-loaded local Boot resources with stable source/document ownership. Current native lane is Boot 2.7.18 / SnakeYAML 1.30, not all Boot versions. Edit the actual runtime file and inspect source precedence.

title: Delete a key or a recognized Boot file
text: Removal reveals lower-priority values/defaults in the supported source path. Mutable property identities are preserved; read-only/write-only removal shapes are uncheckable. Verify resulting defaults and supported consumer rebinding.

title: Change active documents, imports, profiles or config locations
text: Stable source positions/document activation are prerequisites. Startup config topology is not rebuilt by a value save. Restart with the new startup configuration.

title: Change direct or computed @Value inputs
text: Fields, scalar constructor inputs and supported factory arguments have distinct check/recreation paths. Unsupported expression operations hold the candidate. Check the documented expression/consumer shape before retrying.

title: Edit a property on a loaded ordinary XML bean
text: Resolved local file/context ownership plus supported value shape. Setter errors can preserve metadata but still have application side effects. Inspect the property result and independent-bean diagnostics.

title: Edit existing XML constructor/factory/lifecycle metadata
text: Bounded ordinary singleton recreation, stable concrete type/ownership and supported direct holders. Native observer: Spring 5.3.39 / JDK 21. Check creation/destruction, repaired references and any restore failure.

title: Change XML scope, parent, aliases or creation policy
text: Existing metadata changes such as depends-on/primary/autowire/effective lazy flag are guarded. Supported property edits do not rebuild startup policy. Follow the bean-specific restart diagnostic.

title: Save unchanged unsupported XML definitions
text: A proven unchanged standard definition stays quiet, including known abstract/prototype shapes. Unknown/custom metadata retains conservative diagnostics. Expect no reconstruction; real unsupported edits still require restart.

title: Edit newly imported, remote or packaged XML
text: Captured-local discovery does not cover remote/JAR resources, pre-hook loads or a general import-topology rebuild. Edit the actually owned local resource or restart.

title: Edit recognized physical message bundles
text: Named native Spring message-source/cache lanes; arbitrary custom basenames and automatic source-to-output copying are not established. Edit the runtime file and check a warmed formatted lookup.

title: Edit recognized file templates
text: Named FreeMarker/Thymeleaf file-resolver lanes. Malformed saves can produce render errors; last-valid retention is not promised. Render the current output; fix malformed input and retry.

title: Edit resources inside packaged JAR/WAR files
text: Physical-file observers do not establish packaged-resource replacement or arbitrary view-resolver integration. Use unpacked recognized runtime resources or restart/redeploy.

title: Change a supported logging level/configuration
text: Supported logging.level keys or logback/log4j2 config refresh. Removing a level without a fallback can still need reset/restart. Verify the target logger; keep SAP property pairs separate.

title: Expect arbitrary files to trigger a reload
text: ChangeKind recognizes specific suffixes and owned resources. Unknown kinds have no Reclazz reload action; another framework may independently serve the file. Check the resource classifier and your application’s own resource pipeline.

title: Add a mapped field to an existing entity
text: Requires enhanced visibility plus supported jpaRefresh=true/DDL-enabled mapping path; stock companion fields are not native ORM members. Prepare schema/mapping prerequisites or restart.

title: Add a new JPA entity with a prepared schema
text: jpaRefresh=true, explicit Hibernate validate, one unit and standard provider/factory in the recorded graph. No automatic migration or update-mode switch. Prepare table/columns, compile and verify native mapping installation.

title: Retry a new-entity mapping after a schema failure
text: Failed candidate leaves the previous factory open before install. Identical bytes are ignored; changing pending mapping declarations is refused. Fix schema, then compile a body-only edit to the same pending entity.

title: Keep old persistence contexts/transactions through a rebuild
text: A successful persistence-unit swap retires the old native factory. Holding active old contexts across it is unsupported. Finish database work first; restart/recover unsupported retained contexts.

title: Edit supported Spring Data query methods
text: Warm singleton Repository products and bounded direct holder repair. Scalar H2 native-query evidence does not cover new interface methods/all query shapes. Check the query result and the retained managed consumer.

title: Invalidate caches dependent on changed helper code
text: Observed synchronous Spring cache dependencies in stock companion mode; region-level conservative eviction. Async/unwatched/pre-attach work is not complete. Exercise the cache first, reload and check next-call freshness.

title: Rebuild a custom cache owner after helper changes
text: refreshOwnersOnHelper opt-in for supported singleton owners. Non-singletons, FactoryBeans and event-listener owners are declined. Name the eligible owner and check lifecycle/state reset.

title: Save *-items.xml / *-beans.xml
text: Platform generation/build can reload generated classes. Persistence/type-system updates and native reflection are separate requirements. Verify generated bytecode; update the platform schema when required.

title: Create columns through Update Running System
text: Manual HAC action is separate from reload. autoUpdateRunningSystem=true is a distinct off-by-default dev-only DDL opt-in. Choose the schema action explicitly and verify the type/persistence result.

title: Apply changed SAP configuration keys
text: Changed keys reach the Config path; successful keys acknowledge independently. Startup-only consumers are still reported as restart-required. Check each key’s runtime consumer and pending status.

title: Edit type/enum localization or Backoffice labels
text: Recognized physical locale/label files refresh the platform caches they serve. Broader tenant/cluster acceptance is not implied. Check a new lookup or reopen the affected Backoffice view.

title: Import a changed ImpEx file automatically
text: autoImpex=true opt-in writes live development data. REMOVE/macro-expanded REMOVE is refused unless separately permitted; no rollback. Use disposable data; inspect import results and guard diagnostics.

title: Refresh supported interceptor mappings
text: Mappings are captured before bean refresh and re-registered in the actual SAP registry. SDK contract is not live model-save tenant acceptance. Check the registry result and a relevant live model operation.

title: Edit OCC field sets, mappings or supported directives
text: Dedicated field-set/request-mapping/populator/list-merge paths have individual ownership and registration limits. Not arbitrary platform topology reload. Read the matching path and verify the actual OCC response.

title: Add an extension to the platform
text: The extension list is established at startup. Generated-bytecode reload does not enroll a new extension. Build the platform and restart.

title: Edit *-backoffice-config.xml
text: The source resets supported CockpitConfigurationService caches through Resettable.reset, without resetToDefaults. Packaged module copies can still answer until rebuilt. Reopen the view and verify the actual loaded configuration; build a packaged copy if needed.

title: Add a Backoffice @SocketEvent action
text: Requires an agent-prepared class; standard modules follow the backoffice-module admission conditions. Generic reflection lets newly composed default MVC components bind public non-static handlers with at most one parameter. One-parameter native detached dispatch measured on JDK17/21; local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified a new view binding, retained open-view binding, body edit and removal without stale dispatch. Open components retain bindings. Compose a new view. Invalid native signatures keep PENDING; static reload is unverified and keeps PENDING. Removed added methods stop stale dispatch.

title: Reload a Java Backoffice module
text: Explicit backoffice-module=true metadata, selected extension and exact WidgetClassLoader; one owning backoffice/classes file with identical initial bytes. Source compilation and IDE output saves are tested with a synthetic opaque loader; preparation and added-method reload measured with both native SDK loaders. Start with the agent before the class loads. Rebuild stale output/JAR bytes and restart if initial admission fails. Duplicate definitions remain unprepared; reload targets only the prepared owner. Local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified startup preparation and source-to-widget handler add/edit/removal; broader widget routing remains unverified.

title: Edit a registered local SAP process definition XML
text: The agent must observe the native initial resource load. With the SAP automation module and the standard native factory/cache/reader, a valid edit with the original name updates the active definition while preserving historical versions. Renames, duplicate names, active DynamicProcessDefinition rows, custom factories and missing startup observations are refused. Created/deleted resources still require restart. Start with the agent before definitions load. Verify a newly started process; already started processes keep their version within this JVM. Process restart, cache eviction, server restart and cluster propagation are outside this guarantee.

title: Add a new dependency JAR to the JVM classpath
text: The running JVM startup classpath is not replaced by watching class outputs. Restart with the updated launch classpath.

title: Refresh stored documents after an indexing provider/resolver reload
text: autoSolrReindex=true, SAP module, exact provider metadata, stock local standalone provider/strategy, explicit stored PKs and 10,000-document limit. Property providers use partial updates; type resolvers use whole-document UPDATE. Normal native listeners and operation bookkeeping still run. Verify the stored search field separately from the class reload receipt. Unknown targets, missing cores, remote/cluster mode and incomplete reads are refused.

title: Avoid a supported request crossing a method-body reload
text: reloadBoundary=request at startup, supported native MVC hook/lifetimes. Drain deadline defers; it is not batch/schema/background atomicity. Check the measured servlet graph and queued-work diagnostics.

title: Apply class output from a failed/paused build
text: Build admission holds output until a successful captured batch; SCAN alone cannot release the hold. Manual pause is an independent switch. Complete the build, release the correct hold and verify completion.

title: Will your change reload?
text: Start with the change, then read its conditions. A reloaded class does not automatically mean refreshed framework metadata or a changed database schema. Scope travels with the claim These outcomes come from the canonical support reference . Consult the evidence baseline for measured runtime lanes. They are not a promise for every release, framework version or object shape. Read the evidence model. title: When a change spans more than one row
text: When a change spans more than one row Apply the most restrictive relevant condition. Adding a model field can combine a supported bytecode change, a reflection restriction and a required schema update. Check each layer, then verify the runtime behavior. A partial or refused framework step should stay visible in the pending ledger. “No reload” means this path applies no Reclazz change, including a valid no-op save or an unhandled file kind. “Unverified” is a missing acceptance result. It does not mean a feature always fails, and it should not be presented as guaranteed support. Use the pinned technical reference for version-specific test provenance.

title: Java changes & JVM limits
text: Method bodies: the everyday loop Compile a supported change to a watched class and the agent replaces its implementation in the running JVM. Existing object fields remain on a method-body-only path. Core fixtures observe repeated parent/child virtual dispatch and super calls without a new process. Use this as your first verification case before trying structural or framework changes. A bytecode change can succeed while a later framework refresh fails; check the full outcome. Read the technical reference ↗ Add and remove members on a stock JDK Reclazz’s companion engine supports added/removed methods and fields without requiring a patched JVM. Hot-compiled calls to new methods and supported direct field accesses are routed through the companion. Compile affected watched callers too. The original Class does not gain those members on a stock JVM. Arbitrary Class.getMethod / getDeclaredField consumers cannot discover them. Existing object fields remain on a method-body-only path. Core fixtures observe repeated parent/child virtual dispatch and super calls without a new process. Use this as your first verification case before trying structural or framework changes. A bytecode change can succeed while a later framework refresh fails; check the full outcome. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Add and remove members on a stock JDK
text: Add and remove members on a stock JDK Reclazz’s companion engine supports added/removed methods and fields without requiring a patched JVM. Hot-compiled calls to new methods and supported direct field accesses are routed through the companion. Compile affected watched callers too. The original Class does not gain those members on a stock JVM. Arbitrary Class.getMethod / getDeclaredField consumers cannot discover them. Supported framework adapters, such as the documented Jackson path, are explicit exceptions. When a member is removed, scans stop seeing it. A caller that still uses a removed method gets what a restart would give it: NoSuchMethodError , or the inherited implementation when the method was an override. JBR / DCEVM use a different path Enhanced redefinition can expose added members natively. Only use -XX:+AllowEnhancedClassRedefinition with a runtime that supports it. That flag is not valid on a stock OpenJDK installation. Read the technical reference ↗

title: New instance fields on existing objects
text: New instance fields on existing objects On the stock companion path, an isolated initializer can run for each existing object on that field’s first read. It may use that object’s existing state. A later save preserves a value already initialized or written, including null . Java · supported isolated initializers private final List<String> cache = new ArrayList<>(); private int retries = 3; Conditional initializers have a bounded single-constructor path. Constructor-argument dependencies, entangled writes and unsupported instruction shapes cannot be inferred safely: the field retains its type default and the diagnostic names why. Separately reloaded watched callers can share the owner’s added-field store in the recorded SapMachine 17/21 lanes. This does not certify field-type changes or every inherited-field/classloader shape. Enhanced JVMs have real fields; objects created before that reload retain native type defaults. Read the technical reference ↗

title: New static fields and constants
text: New static fields and constants A compile-time constant or an isolated static initializer can initialize an added static field. Supported forward conditional/switch expressions execute only the selected arm. Existing static blocks and values are not reset, and changing an initializer later does not reinitialize a field already populated. Loops, inseparable side effects and unsupported control flow leave the added field at its type default and produce a reason. A compile-time constant already inlined into callers needs those callers rebuilt; AutoCompile can rebuild detected watched sources. Unwatched consumers are outside that repair. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Enums: preserve ordinals
text: Enums: preserve ordinals Appending a constant and removing the final constant have documented support on JDK 17–25, including values() , valueOf , switches and existing EnumMap/EnumSet instances. Arrays your application sized from the old enum length remain the old size. Insertion, reordering and non-tail removal renumber ordinals and are refused. Restart for the change and account separately for persisted ordinal data. Do not infer coverage of a newer JDK from the target Java version. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Interfaces and superclass edits
text: Interfaces and superclass edits Adding or removing implemented interfaces requires a compatible enhanced-redefinition JVM. On a stock JVM, the interface change is refused. Reclazz does not apply a new superclass. Eligible method bodies may reload while retaining the old hierarchy; methods dependent on the changed parent remain pinned. Unsafe signatures or constructors can refuse the whole save. Restart to complete the hierarchy change and inspect partial/refused reporting. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Spring beans & web behavior
text: Bean refresh has a lifecycle After a supported class reload, Spring integration can destroy and recreate affected singletons, clear metadata caches and repair supported direct references. This differs from retaining the original instance after a method-body-only JVM redefinition. Creation/destruction callbacks can run and mutable state can reset. External holders, local variables, arbitrary nested object graphs, static/final fields and every possible proxy shape are not a universal reference-repair surface. Read the technical reference ↗ New components and factory methods A newly compiled component can register through direct/composed stereotypes using Spring’s name, scope and condition machinery. Singleton/prototype and lazy behavior follow native creation policy. Class-level profiles/conditions are checked at registration time. This is not a repeat of startup scanning: imports, auto-configuration ordering, custom scan filters, web/custom scopes and scoped proxies remain outside that addition. Previously filtered components are not generally rediscovered by a later property/profile save. Supported newly added @Bean factories can take reference beans, typed collections/maps, arrays

External holders, local variables, arbitrary nested object graphs, static/final fields and every possible proxy shape are not a universal reference-repair surface. Read the technical reference ↗

title: New components and factory methods
text: New components and factory methods A newly compiled component can register through direct/composed stereotypes using Spring’s name, scope and condition machinery. Singleton/prototype and lazy behavior follow native creation policy. Class-level profiles/conditions are checked at registration time. This is not a repeat of startup scanning: imports, auto-configuration ordering, custom scan filters, web/custom scopes and scoped proxies remain outside that addition. Previously filtered components are not generally rediscovered by a later property/profile save. Supported newly added @Bean factories can take reference beans, typed collections/maps, arrays, Optional, providers and direct @Value inputs. Alias names, direct selection metadata, lazy/prototype behavior, profiles and documented direct conditions have bounded support. Existing names are refused; removal only deletes Reclazz-owned registrations. Lite and full configuration paths differ. Default configuration supports eligible overridable instance factories and container-backed inter-bean calls; static factories keep ordinary Java call semantics. Read the exact allowlist before using composed conditions, custom scopes or proxy shapes. Read the technical reference ↗ Component registration details ↗

title: Endpoints, exception handling and binding
text: Endpoints, exception handling and binding Supported structural controller changes rescan request mappings, including added endpoints. Plain controller/advice adapters can expose added @ExceptionHandler , @InitBinder and @ModelAttribute callbacks even on stock JVMs. Spring retains handler selection, local priority, advice selectors/order and supported parameter conversion. Ambiguous handler mappings are rejected. Proxied/subclass receivers, inherited/generic/composed shapes, asynchronous/streaming added exception handlers and custom resolvers fall outside their documented adapter scope. A hidden metadata delegate is visible to the framework. Custom argument/response code that requires the original declaring-class identity needs separate validation. Registered MVC interceptors have a distinct current-singleton routing path; arbitrary interceptor-registry rebuilding is not implied. Read the technical reference ↗ Binding and model scope ↗ Registered interceptor scope ↗

title: Transactions, caching, security and async
text: Transactions, caching, security and async Supported added public service methods use the application’s real transaction/cache interceptors. Supported composed transaction/cache metadata and direct or bounded composed pre/post authorization are documented separately. Existing CGLIB references are covered in named tests; arbitrary extra advice shapes are refused. Added direct public @Async service methods support void, Future and CompletableFuture return paths with the application’s executor/error handling. Method-security metadata and supported existing proxy chains are refreshed. An edited @Aspect pointcut updates supported mutable singleton proxies; a previously unproxied object is a separate limit. These are scoped adapters, not permission to bypass an unknown proxy. Verify both success and denial/rollback/cache behavior relevant to the edit. Read the technical reference ↗ Security scope ↗ Async scope ↗ Aspect scope ↗

title: Scheduling, events and lifecycle callbacks
text: Scheduling, events and lifecycle callbacks Supported added no-argument void @Scheduled methods register with Spring; later edits replace registrations and removal cancels them. Direct @EventListener additions accept one reference event input and void or one event-object return. Supported transaction/cache and void async combinations have separate allowlists. Added direct void @TransactionalEventListener methods use Spring’s transaction phases on supported unproxied singletons. Added lifecycle callbacks initialize new instances after injection; each instance retains the added destroy callback it was initialized with through later edits and removal. Read the technical reference ↗ Event listener scope ↗ Transactional event scope ↗ Lifecycle scope ↗

title: Jackson DTO shape changes
text: Jackson DTO shape changes Within the documented Spring-managed mapper adapter, added getters, void setters and instance fields participate in JSON output/input on mutable DTOs. Saved annotations, aliases, naming/null rules and serializers/deserializers remain with Jackson. Later saves can rename, remove and restore properties. Final added fields cannot be written. Constructor/record creators, builders, arbitrary mapper instances and other serializers are not covered by that addition. The native HTTP baseline uses Jackson 2.13.5. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Constructor-captured helper values
text: Constructor-captured helper values The source baseline contains a bounded ordinary helper → constructor-injected leaf-owner transaction, including one measured direct-child context shape. It refreshes supported constructor-captured values and writable singleton holders using native dependency registration. It requires exact supported factory versions and plain definitions. Aliases, transitive/multiple dependents, proxies, factory products, annotated injection/lifecycle state and arbitrary parent hierarchies are excluded. Synthetic SDK-derived Spring graphs are not a live SAP tenant/cluster acceptance claim. JMS, Kafka and Rabbit have separately measured, bounded consumer transactions. The Rabbit helper/property path is limited to one root context, one plain local helper and leaf owner, one void literal-ID callback and standard native AUTO acknowledgment with nontransacted channels; see the pinned framework versions and exclusions in the technical reference. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Validation and HTTP security metadata
text: Validation and HTTP security metadata Reloading a constraint annotation alone can leave a provider serving cached validation metadata. The supported Hibernate Validator path clears owned metadata caches and discovers both javax and Jakarta factory names. Check a failing input and a valid control after a constraint edit; a different validator/provider shape needs its own acceptance. An edited supported security configuration rebuilds its SecurityFilterChain beans and updates the existing FilterChainProxy, retaining inline ignoring chains. A failed rebuild can leave old rules serving, so class reload alone is not evidence that an authorization change is live. Verify allowed and denied requests. This differs from the added service-method security adapter. Validator cache scope ↗ Filter-chain implementation ↗ Native HTTP rule observer ↗

title: Messaging without blind spots
text: Start with configured messaging infrastructure Reclazz can add supported listener methods to already-running plain singleton components. It uses your application’s native listener processors, factories and conversion. Compile the listener change and inspect both registration and delivery. Use explicit stable listener IDs. Original consumers are retired before a replacement bean is created, and unrelated registry entries are preserved. Proxies, custom adapters, mixed broker ownership and unsupported factory shapes can require restart. A class-body reload may already have happened when listener follow-up fails. Delivery semantics still belong to your application Consumer coordination does not make reload atomic or guarantee exactly-once delivery. Offsets, acknowledgments, transactions, retries and broker redelivery still matter. title: Kafka: topics, groups and native dispatch
text: Kafka: topics, groups and native dispatch Java · existing plain component @KafkaListener(id = "orders-created", topics = "orders", groupId = "orders-service") public void onOrder(String payload) { processOrder(payload); } Added public/private void instance callbacks support native payload/header conversion. Topics and groups accept their documented literal, placeholder and expression forms; __listener resolves against the real singleton. Literal factory, concurrency, idIsGroup and autoStartup options have bounded support. Re-save the listener to reevaluate its route. Changing only a routing bean or property is not a general reroute trigger. An expression error after retirement can leave the new registration absent; save a valid listener to retry. Changing the consumer group can replay retained records. Use the standard record-mode factory and registry. Batch callbacks, retry/filter/customized factories, arbitrary advice and repeatable/class-level additions are excluded. Stop callbacks must finish within the 30-second wait; otherwise follow-up is deferred and ownership retained. Named direct lanes: Kafka 2.9.13 / Framework 5.3.39 / embedded Kafka 3.2.3, and Kafka 3.2.4 / Framework 6.1.14 / embedded Kafka 3.7.1, on stock JDK 17/21. Read the technical reference ↗

title: JMS: destinations and synchronous replies
text: JMS: destinations and synchronous replies Java · supported reply shape @JmsListener(id = "order-status", destination = "order-status-requests") @SendTo("${order.status.replies}") public String status(String orderId) { return findOrderStatus(orderId); } Added callbacks support the documented void/text/bytes/map/native-message/Spring-message results. A non-null reply uses the request’s JMSReplyTo ahead of direct method @SendTo ; null sends nothing. Spring retains correlation and conversion. Destination and selector placeholders are supported; SpEL destinations, XA, durable/shared topics, custom factories/executors and proxy receivers are outside this addition. Native message types differ between javax and Jakarta lanes. Do not generalize the allowed result types to arbitrary DTO, Future or reactive returns. Named lanes: Framework/JMS 5.3.39 with ActiveMQ Classic 5.19.11, and Framework/JMS 6.1.14 with Jakarta Messaging 3.1.0 / ActiveMQ Classic 6.1.3, on stock JDK 17/21. Modern native-message and String reply observers are recorded separately. Read the technical reference ↗

title: RabbitMQ: wait for the actual workers
text: RabbitMQ: wait for the actual workers Java · existing plain component @RabbitListener(id = "orders-created", queues = "orders") public void onOrder(String payload) { processOrder(payload); } Added public/private void callbacks support literal, property and documented SpEL queue values, including names and native Queue objects resolved by Spring. Existing original listeners may retain generated IDs; newly added callbacks require an explicit nonempty literal ID. Use standard simple containers with AUTO acknowledgment and the default SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor. Newly added consumers require the standard simple factory without a customizer. Local channel transactions are supported. Direct/stream/batch containers, custom executors, external transactions, inline binding declarations, method advice and added return/reply/async callbacks are excluded. The startup hook tracks real workers through complete exit. A zero consumer count alone is not sufficient. Retirement waits up to 30 seconds for destruction and worker completion; timeout/interruption preserves registry ownership and defers recreation. A later direct class save waits for the same retirement. Named direct lanes: Spring Rabbit 2.4.17 / Framework 5.3.39 and Rabbit 3.1.7 / Framework 6.1.14, RabbitMQ 4.3.5, stock JDK 17/21 on macOS arm64. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A helper or property save is a separate feature
text: A helper or property save is a separate feature JMS, Kafka and Rabbit each have a separately measured transaction for reconstructing a plain local leaf listener after a helper-body or scalar helper-constructor property edit. Each transaction has its own root-context, factory, owner and callback restrictions in the constructor dependency guide. The Rabbit indirect path is measured on Framework 5.3.39/AMQP 2.4.17 and Framework 6.1.14/AMQP 3.1.7, stock JDK 17/21 on macOS arm64. It requires one plain local helper/leaf owner, one void callback with a literal ID, standard native simple containers, AUTO acknowledgment and nontransacted channels. Direct listener reload support for local channel transactions does not extend to this helper/property path. Complete worker retirement precedes reconstruction; a stop timeout or partial reconstruction requires restart. These bounded observations do not establish arbitrary indirect listener graph refresh, distributed delivery or exactly-once behavior. Rabbit helper/property scope → Read the technical reference ↗

title: Verify the consumer, not just the class
text: Verify the consumer, not just the class Record the original listener ID, route and a uniquely identifiable test message. Compile the change and wait for framework follow-up. Send a new test message and check the expected handler result. For a route change, check both the new route and retirement of the old consumer. Inspect diagnostics before retrying a partial registration or retirement timeout. Use disposable development data: a valid retry can redeliver messages, and saving old source does not undo application side effects.

title: Configuration, XML & resources
text: Properties: validate before applying In the non-SAP Boot path, a saved candidate is bound/converted/validated on separate objects before changing live values. If a timeout is invalid, another valid key in that candidate does not get applied first. Fix the invalid value and save again to retry the pending keys. application.properties · illustrative keys svc.url=https://example.com/api svc.timeout=30 A clean precheck is not rollback for arbitrary constructors, converters, validators or setters. Application-time failures can partially change values and are reported as partial. Uncheckable candidates keep the old values and remain pending. Direct @Value fields can update in place; supported constructor-bound and factory-argument consumers can be recreated. Computed expressions have a restricted evaluator/check path. A connection pool or other startup-only consumer is not automatically rebuilt because the Environment changed. Read the technical reference ↗ YAML, removed keys and source precedence Already-loaded local Boot properties/YAML resources are identified from native origins. Supported saves replace those sources at their existing precedence positions. Higher-priority command-lin

title: YAML, removed keys and source precedence
text: YAML, removed keys and source precedence Already-loaded local Boot properties/YAML resources are identified from native origins. Supported saves replace those sources at their existing precedence positions. Higher-priority command-line values still win; an inactive profile file is not promoted into a new override. Deleting a key can reveal a lower-priority value or default. Mutable property beans retain their identity through supported removal rebinding, though nested objects can be replaced. Emptying/deleting/restoring a recognized single-document resource has a bounded path. Malformed input and invalid conversion preserve old sources. Changing config imports/locations, profile activation/groups, cloud-platform selection or the active document set needs restart. New/unowned resources, custom loaders and changed source ownership are outside that path. Exact version coverage matters The current P5 native Boot file evidence is Boot 2.7.18 / Framework 5.3.39 / SnakeYAML 1.30 on SapMachine 17/21. A broader current Boot 3 YAML graph is not certified by those results. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Spring XML: loaded resource ownership
text: Spring XML: loaded resource ownership Alongside *-spring.xml , the agent captures local XML files actually loaded by a live context after its reader hook starts, including nested imports. It uses resolved file and context ownership, not just the filename. Supported property edits update ordinary beans in place. A resolution, conversion or setter failure retains the previous raw property definition and reports the failure; independent properties/beans may still update. Setter side effects are not rolled back. Cold lazy beans retain native deferred validation. Captured files outside watch roots are polled individually. JAR entries, remote XML and files loaded before the hook are not included. A new import topology is not a complete live context rebuild. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Existing XML singletons: bounded recreation
text: Existing XML singletons: bounded recreation Supported changes to existing constructor arguments, public factory selection and explicit init/destroy metadata can recreate a plain singleton through Spring. Writable direct singleton-holder fields can be repaired; supported plain dependents are recreated too. Unchanged definitions do not trigger recreation. Preflight requires the same concrete product type, exact file ownership and stable class/factory-bean/alias metadata. FactoryBean products, resource owners such as DataSource/Executor/AutoCloseable, proxies and unsupported nested compositions are refused. Known final or collection/map/array holders block the supported recreation path before destruction. Changes to scope, parent, alias, depends-on, primary, autowire/autowire-candidate or effective lazy policy require the reported restart. New constructor/factory/lifecycle definitions and bean removal remain outside the recreation increment. A proven unchanged unsupported definition stays quiet on a no-op save. On failed creation, restoration can be attempted and can fail itself. It is not rollback of lifecycle or constructor side effects. The recreation extension is observed on Spring 5.3.39 / JDK 21, including child loaders; other versions/SAP runtime/JDK 17 require separate proof for that extension. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Message bundles and templates
text: Message bundles and templates Recognized physical message resources invalidate native caches. Current evidence observes ResourceBundleMessageSource and ReloadableResourceBundleMessageSource on Framework 5.3.39/6.1.14, including UTF-8 and fallback keys. Arbitrary custom message basenames are not automatically discovered. Native file-template rendering is observed with FreeMarker 2.3.34 and Thymeleaf 3.1.3.RELEASE with FileTemplateResolver/standard dialect. A malformed template can fail rendering; fixing it recovers. Last-valid-template retention is not promised. Edit the actual runtime resource. Automatic copying from a source resource directory, packaged JAR/WAR resources, custom resolvers/dialects and full MVC view integration are not established by these fixtures. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Logging configuration
text: Logging configuration Supported logging.level.* properties and saved logback.xml / log4j2.xml can update the running logging context. Removal without a lower configured level can still require a reset/restart. On SAP Commerce, use the platform logger-property pair described in its guide. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Recognition is not universal file watching
text: Recognition is not universal file watching The source classifier sends recognized kinds to different handlers. Recognition still needs an enabled handler, a watched/owned physical resource and its documented framework prerequisites. Source-classified file families File or ownership Meaning .class / .java Compiled reload / optional source compilation. Without AutoCompile, build the source yourself. *-spring.xml or captured local Spring XML Guarded bean-definition path, not arbitrary XML topology refresh. *-items.xml / *-beans.xml SAP code generation; schema and reflection remain separate. .properties / .yml / .yaml Platform-specific configuration; recognized message/locale names take priority. messages[_locale].properties / ValidationMessages[_locale].properties Text/cache invalidation, not general Environment configuration. .ftl , .ftlh , .html , .htm Template handler classification; only the documented engine/resolver lanes are accepted. Recognized Logback / Log4j2 XML names Logging reconfiguration, ahead of generic XML rules. .impex Opt-in live import with separate REMOVE permission. *-backoffice-config.xml / owned process XML Backoffice cache reset / process diagnostic-only path, respectively. Unknown kinds No Reclazz handler. Another framework may independently serve them; that is separate behavior. Exact filename and ownership rules ↗

title: SAP Commerce: keep the server warm
text: Attach through platform-owned launch configuration Use Java 17+ and a matching agent. Put a stable agent path in hybris/config/local.properties through tomcat.javaoptions , preserving any existing JVM options. local.properties · merge with existing options tomcat.javaoptions=-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar Do not self-reference tomcat.generaloptions . Do not rely on directly editing generated tomcat/conf/wrapper.conf : ant server regenerates it. The IDE integration can manage the same platform property for you. Start once with the configured agent, then compile edited Java with the platform build. Enabling a plugin cannot instrument a server process that was already launched externally. Read the technical reference ↗ Generated model and DTO changes Saving *-items.xml or *-beans.xml can run platform generation/build and reload the generated bytecode. That saves a restart for the supported Java change; it does not by itself create a database column or complete every platform type-system action. title: Generated model and DTO changes
text: Generated model and DTO changes Saving *-items.xml or *-beans.xml can run platform generation/build and reload the generated bytecode. That saves a restart for the supported Java change; it does not by itself create a database column or complete every platform type-system action. Edit XML → Platform generation → Reload bytecode → Verify persistence separately For a new persistent attribute, perform the required Update Running System in HAC. Original-class reflective dispatch to added members still follows the stock/enhanced JVM limits. ModelService/Groovy reflective paths on a stock JVM may need enhanced redefinition or restart. Schema updates are an explicit opt-in autoUpdateRunningSystem=true adds a development-only schema update path after items generation. Its default is false. It runs DDL against the live database; generation and ordinary reload do not imply that this option is enabled. Read the technical reference ↗ Generation and restart boundaries ↗

title: Properties, localization and Backoffice
text: Properties, localization and Backoffice Changed SAP configuration keys are applied through the platform Config path. Successfully applied keys are acknowledged independently; failed keys stay pending for retry. A startup-only consumer still needs its reported restart. This differs from the Boot candidate-binding path. Platform log levels use log4j2.logger.<key>.name and .level pairs. Only touched loggers are updated, preserving unrelated HAC changes. Type/enum locale resources refresh localization caches; Backoffice label resources refresh the relevant label caches. Reopen the affected view to check the result. Supported Spring XML bean changes follow the XML safety rules. Recognizing an XML file does not imply arbitrary MVC/security/filter-chain reconstruction. Read the technical reference ↗ SAP outcomes and retry behavior ↗

title: ImpEx changes write real data
text: ImpEx changes write real data autoImpex=true is off by default. If enabled, recognized changed ImpEx files import into the running database. There is no automatic undo of application or import side effects. Literal and macro-expanded REMOVE headers are refused unless impexAllowRemove=true . Unresolved/recursive header macros are also refused. This bounded scan is not a full ImpEx parser or an executable-script sandbox. Use HAC when the scan cannot establish the header’s safety. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Know the platform boundary
text: Know the platform boundary A new extension changes the startup extension list: build and restart. New dependency JARs change the JVM classpath: restart. Database/data migration, tenant initialization and cluster-wide consistency are separate responsibilities. Interceptor refresh captures mappings before bean refresh and updates the actual SAP registry afterward. Missing/failed registration is a diagnostic, not success. SDK contract evidence must be distinguished from a live model-save/tenant acceptance test. OCC field sets, request mappings/overrides and populator/list-merge directives have dedicated support paths. Read their detailed scope before changing registry topology or assuming an arbitrary custom composition is covered. OCC field-set scope ↗ OCC request mapping scope ↗ Populator and list-merge scope ↗

title: Backoffice configuration and process definitions
text: Backoffice configuration and process definitions A recognized *-backoffice-config.xml save resets supported cockpit configuration caches through the native Resettable.reset() contract. It does not call resetToDefaults() or erase user customizations. If the running module reads a packaged copy, rebuild that copy before expecting the new configuration on view open. The implementation path is distinct from live tenant acceptance. Widget action rules require an agent-prepared class. Standard module admission is described below. Existing prepared widget action bodies use ordinary class reload. Generic reflection already lets newly composed default MVC components bind added public non-static @SocketEvent handlers with at most one parameter; open components retain their bindings. Native SDK dispatch was measured for one-parameter handlers on JDK17/21 with actual cockpitng listeners and detached ZK components. A local Chrome acceptance on 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified a self-connected synthetic widget: a newly composed second-tab view bound the added handler, the open view kept its binding, body edits applied, and removal stopped stale dispatch. Arbitrary socket/connection routing, MVVM and other reopen workflows remain unverified. Invalid native signatures keep a pending finding; static companion reload is unverified and also keeps a finding. Removing an added method now stops held listeners from running its stale body; restoring the signature restores its dispatch. Label/config cache refresh does not install actions, and no whole-helper replay or user configuration reset is performed. Start with Reclazz before SAP first loads process definitions. A valid edit to an observed, registered local process XML can update its active in-memory definition through the native factory. Newly started processes use the edited graph; already started processes keep their stored definition version in that JVM. Renamed processes, duplicate resource names, active DynamicProcessDefinition rows, custom factory/cache/reader implementations and files whose initial load was not observed are refused with a restart explanation. Created and deleted resources still require restart. A save before the native lazy cache first loads is left for that native load to read. This does not migrate, replay or restart a process. Backoffice process restart, cache eviction, server restart and cluster propagation are outside the version-retention guarantee. Native parser/cache checks and a synthetic watcher fixture are separate from live tenant acceptance; see the evidence record for the current verification state. Backoffice cache implementation ↗ Widget action boundary ↗ Process recognition/refusal fixture ↗

title: Stored Solr documents after a provider edit
text: Stored Solr documents after a provider edit Provider code already reloads for subsequent indexing calls. With autoSolrReindex=true , the SAP module can also queue a native update of existing local search documents. The default stays off. The update selects only types and properties whose provider metadata matches the changed class, uses the stored PKs from the active physical index and refuses more than 10,000 stored documents per type. Property providers use a partial update; type-level resolvers use a whole-document UPDATE. No FULL operation, schema change, core reload or index switch is requested. Only the stock local standalone provider and indexer strategy are supported. Unknown metadata, remote or distributed targets, missing cores and incomplete reads are refused. Discovery uses persisted provider identifiers and bean type metadata without loading native configurations or creating providers. Once targets are known, native preparation runs in a fresh tenant session; configuration loading, including physical-ownership checks, can construct providers. Persisted/native mapping mismatches are refused. Normal platform listeners and operation bookkeeping still run, including project callbacks and native database writes. Native indexing recalculates current values. Live type-level evidence uses a provider implementing both modern and legacy interfaces, with the legacy native callback selected; modern-only native acceptance remains unverified. The class reload receipt remains separate from indexing: verify the served search field after the operation. Scope, refusals and outcome wording ↗ Unit, watcher, SDK and live verification status ↗

title: Java Backoffice modules
text: Java Backoffice modules Extensions with explicit backoffice-module=true metadata can compile saved backoffice/src sources or reload IDE builds in backoffice/classes . Core outputs and required Backoffice module classpaths stay separate. Start with the agent before the widget class loads. The standard WidgetClassLoader qualifies only with one selected owning output file and identical initial bytes. A stale JAR/output mismatch, duplicate owner or another loader is refused. Subsequent saves target the prepared loader only; deployed JARs are not rewritten. Restart with matching startup artifacts if preparation was missed. Synthetic watcher tests and both native SDK loader checks cover the Java reload path. Independent live Chrome acceptance on local 2211-jdk21.8/JDK21 verified startup preparation, source compilation, new-view versus open-view binding, handler body edits and removal without stale dispatch. The accepted flow is a self-connected synthetic widget with the default MVC binder; broader widget routing, static handlers and other live platform/JDK combinations remain unverified. Module conditions and verification ↗

title: Persistence & cache boundaries
text: Four things to check separately Bytecode: did the class change in the JVM? Mapping: does the persistence unit recognize the new shape? Schema: does the database have the required table/column? Consumers: are the repositories, EntityManagers and caches using the intended state? Success at one layer is not proof of all four. The JVM staying alive says nothing by itself about open database work surviving a persistence-unit rebuild. Read the technical reference ↗ Existing JPA entities Class method changes can reload without rebuilding every ORM mapping. A new field on an existing entity needs enhanced-redefinition visibility for the documented jpaRefresh=true mapping-refresh path. That option is false by default. With supported DDL-enabled settings such as update/create/create-drop, rebuilding the persistence unit can perform the configured schema action. In other cases the agent identifies the field and required action; it does not silently turn validation into schema creation. Old open persistence contexts are not retained across a successful rebuild. Finish active database work before triggering it. On a stock JVM, existing-entity field additions still need enhanced redefinition or

title: Existing JPA entities
text: Existing JPA entities Class method changes can reload without rebuilding every ORM mapping. A new field on an existing entity needs enhanced-redefinition visibility for the documented jpaRefresh=true mapping-refresh path. That option is false by default. With supported DDL-enabled settings such as update/create/create-drop, rebuilding the persistence unit can perform the configured schema action.
