Old open persistence contexts are not retained across a successful rebuild. Finish active database work before triggering it. On a stock JVM, existing-entity field additions still need enhanced redefinition or restart for ORM mapping. Read the technical reference ↗

title: New entities with a prepared schema
text: New entities with a prepared schema A separate opt-in path supports a new entity on a stock JVM when the table is already prepared and the explicitly selected Hibernate mode is validate . Native validation checks the candidate before installing it; the path does not switch the mode to update/create. The measured path uses one persistence unit, the standard LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean and Hibernate provider. Missing tables/columns or incompatible column types leave the previous factory open before candidate installation. After fixing the schema, compile a body-only edit to the pending entity to retry. Identical class bytes are normally ignored. Changing the pending declarations/mapping is refused: restore the mapping and make the body edit, or restart for the changed mapping. Named evidence uses Spring ORM 6.1.14 / Hibernate 6.5.3.Final / H2 on stock JDK 21; a separate held-repository observer adds stock SapMachine 17/21 coverage. Multiple persistence units, custom providers/schema tools and automatic migrations are outside that acceptance. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Spring Data repositories and held references
text: Spring Data repositories and held references The repository refresh path identifies actual Spring Data Repository types. A plain @Repository DAO follows ordinary bean refresh. Warm singleton repository products can be recreated and supported ordinary singleton fields repaired; cold factories are not eagerly initialized just to discover their type. Query edits have scoped native SQL/JPQL observers. The scalar H2 native-query lane uses Data JPA 3.3.4 / Framework 6.1.14 / Hibernate 6.5.3.Final. It does not certify all database dialects, pagination, projections or newly added repository interface methods. A separate prepared-schema observer retains an existing domain-root repository, shared EntityManager and client factory proxy through a new-entity mapping swap. It does not establish a repository whose own generic domain root becomes a newly added type. Read the technical reference ↗ Held-repository mapping scope ↗

title: Spring caches: follow observed dependencies
text: Spring caches: follow observed dependencies The stock companion path records watched classes executed through Spring’s synchronous cache interceptor and the actual cache instances. A helper edit can invalidate observed dependent regions, including outer caches that read a cached inner result. Regions with the same name in different managers/contexts stay distinct. This is region-level, conservative dependency tracking. Unknown/incomplete history uses the documented fallback for annotated classes. Unwatched code, constructor/static initialization, excluded methods, pre-attach entries and async/reactive cache computations are not fully covered. A computation overlapping reload can return its old result to its caller; exit invalidation prevents retaining it after a successful clear. Other threads may still observe the storage-to-exit interval. This is not a concurrent cache snapshot. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A custom cache needs an explicit owner
text: A custom cache needs an explicit owner refreshOwnersOnHelper can name supported Spring singleton cache-owner classes to recreate after a helper reload. This rebuilds the owner through its ordinary lifecycle; it is not arbitrary cache discovery. Non-singletons, FactoryBeans and event-listener owners are declined. Review recreation state loss and the owner allowlist before opting in. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Reload timing & build safety
text: Default: immediate application The default reloadBoundary=immediate installs no request hook. A request can call old code, cross a reload, then call new code. This is the ordinary reload behavior; application-wide atomicity is not implied. Read the technical reference ↗ Opt in to a supported MVC request boundary shell java "-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=reloadBoundary=request" -jar app.jar Start with the agent before MVC loads. Supported requests finish before the class batch and framework follow-up run; new requests wait during application. The agent waits up to one second to drain active requests, then admits traffic again and retains the edit for a natural idle boundary. The one-second limit applies to draining, not total reload duration. A long framework follow-up can delay new requests for longer. An uncompleted async request or a Callable worker ignoring cancellation can defer reload indefinitely. Native Spring 5 javax / Spring 6 Jakarta MVC dispatches include supported Callable, WebAsyncTask and DeferredResult lifetimes through servlet completion. A timed-out Callable worker remains counted until its body actually exits. The boundary has a measured scope

title: Opt in to a supported MVC request boundary
text: Opt in to a supported MVC request boundary shell java "-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=reloadBoundary=request" -jar app.jar Start with the agent before MVC loads. Supported requests finish before the class batch and framework follow-up run; new requests wait during application. The one-second limit applies to draining, not total reload duration. A long framework follow-up can delay new requests for longer. An uncompleted async request or a Callable worker ignoring cancellation can defer reload indefinitely. Native Spring 5 javax / Spring 6 Jakarta MVC dispatches include supported Callable, WebAsyncTask and DeferredResult lifetimes through servlet completion. A timed-out Callable worker remains counted until its body actually exits. The boundary has a measured scope It covers successful method-body changes through supported MVC lifetimes. Filters outside dispatch, WebFlux, streaming/SSE, background jobs and arbitrary async work are outside that scope. Structural and partially failed batches retain their own limits. Recorded native graphs: Framework 5.3.39 / Tomcat 9.0.121 and Framework 6.1.14 / Tomcat 10.1.60, stock SapMachine 17/21, ordinary/child application loaders. A missing hook defers edits; it does not silently certify request protection. Use immediate mode for a non-MVC application. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A successful build controls admission
text: A successful build controls admission IntelliJ build signals hold class output while compilation is in progress. BUILD ok permits a complete captured batch only after success; a failed/cancelled build keeps it held. Newer build starts/failures invalidate an unfinished capture. SCAN does not release a build hold. Already accepted bytes may finish while the next build is held. AutoCompile stages all modules before publishing output. These controls protect admission; they do not make framework refresh transactional. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Pause is independent of build ownership
text: Pause is independent of build ownership The source baseline includes correlated RELOAD pause , resume and status commands. Wait for the acknowledgement; an old agent can ignore an unsupported command. Pause retains/coalesces newly observed work, but work already admitted can finish. Resume does not unlock an active/failed build hold. Its acknowledgement describes admission state, not completed reload. It does not freeze application requests, stop a classloader loading new disk output, or roll back changes. Read the technical reference ↗

title: A batch can apply partially
text: A batch can apply partially JVM redefinition, framework metadata, singleton lifecycle and external resources are not one transaction. A later step can fail after earlier changes are already live. Read the pending ledger and verify the actual behavior before calling the save complete. Saving the old source can reload the old implementation, but does not recover lost bean state, reverse DDL, undo imported data or restore consumed messages. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Agent configuration reference
text: Agent argument syntax shell java "-javaagent:/absolute/tools/reclazz-agent-X.Y.Z.jar=watchDirs=/absolute/app/target/classes,verbose=true" -jar app.jar Use comma-separated key=value pairs after the agent JAR’s equals sign. Lists use semicolons where documented. Quote the complete agent argument when paths contain spaces. The parser splits commas only where a known key follows; avoid appending unknown keys to another value. These are application-JVM startup options. Match them to the installed agent version. title: Startup options
text: Startup options Accepted keys and documented defaults at 1.5.0 Option Default Behavior and scope hybrisHome auto-detect Absolute path to the hybris/ directory watchExtensions all custom Semicolon-separated extension names to watch (empty = all) excludePatterns (none) Semicolon-separated glob patterns to exclude (e.g., *Test.class;*Mock* ) autoCompile false Compile .java files internally instead of watching .class files autoImpex false Auto-import changed .impex files debounceMs 500 Milliseconds to wait before processing changes (batches rapid file writes) startupDelaySec 30 Seconds to wait after agent startup before watching files verbose false Enable verbose logging in the console, including each framework step's own line after a reload (the reload line carries the summary either way) statusPort 0 TCP port for plugin communication (0 = auto-assign) portFile (none) Path where agent writes its actual port after binding watchDirs auto-detect Semicolon-separated class output directories to watch, for a project the detection does not know excludeClasses (none) Semicolon-separated class name patterns the transform leaves alone; the way out when instrumenting one class is the problem impexAllowRemove false Let auto-imported ImpEx files run REMOVE lines autoUpdateRunningSystem false After an items.xml change regenerates the models, run the schema-only Update Running System (add columns, no data, never drop) so a new attribute is live without a manual HAC click. A saved *-locales_<iso>.properties also writes the type, attribute and enumeration names it keys onto the types, as "Localize types" would for those keys only. Writes to the live database, so opt-in and dev-only autoSolrReindex false After a SAP Commerce indexing provider/resolver reload, queue a bounded native update of its existing local Solr documents. Runs normal platform listeners and bookkeeping. Development only; see targeted reindexing jpaRefresh false Opt-in mapping rebuild. Existing fields require enhanced redefinition; new entities also work on stock JDKs, including supported Hibernate validate with a prepared schema. See scope structuralReload true The companion engine that adds and removes members on a stock JDK; false leaves method-body reloads only platform auto Skip detection and name the platform ( hybris , spring , generic ) wrapOutput auto Wrap console lines to the terminal width: auto , true , false transformDumpDir (none) Write every transformed class file here, for looking at what the agent emitted verifyTransform false Run the bytecode verifier over every transformed class and print what it says sessionLog (none) Append every status line to this file with an ISO timestamp and level, no colour: the session's record, to read back or attach to a report reloadBoundary immediate request waits for synchronous MVC dispatches and supported Spring 5 javax and Spring 6 Jakarta MVC async requests before applying a class reload batch; requires -javaagent at JVM startup. See Reload between requests refreshOwnersOnHelper (none) Opt-in helperFqn>owner1;owner2\|helper2>owner3 : after a helper class reloads, recreate the named Spring singleton cache-owner beans so a custom cache they hold is rebuilt through the fresh helper logic. Owners are recreated through the normal guarded bean-reload lifecycle; non-singletons, FactoryBeans and event-listener owners are declined. See Refreshing a custom cache after a helper reload

title: Defaults keep consequential actions explicit
text: Defaults keep consequential actions explicit Source defaults leave automatic ImpEx import, REMOVE permission, schema updating and JPA mapping refresh disabled. Opting into one does not opt into the others. Read its guide and verify its exact supported lifecycle before enabling it. reloadBoundary=request needs startup attachment and a supported MVC hook. refreshOwnersOnHelper recreates eligible named owners; it does not preserve their instance state. Source of accepted keys and defaults ↗

title: Find the cause. Keep the evidence.
text: “I saved, but nothing changed” Check the target JVM. Confirm that this application started with the intended agent and version. An IDE or MCP connection can target a different process. Check the compiler output. The default route watches compiled files, not editor text. Use the build that writes the configured output directories. Wait for startup. The default watcher delay is 30 seconds. Check admission. A paused agent, failed build hold or deferred request boundary can retain a valid edit. Inspect the class result. Ask DIAGNOSE for the exact class and inspect PENDING for incomplete changes. Check your edit’s scope. Reflection, hierarchy, schema and framework changes can have different results. title: Common symptoms and next steps
text: Common symptoms and next steps New method works in Java but reflection cannot find it On a stock JVM the original Class does not gain companion members. Compile supported watched callers, use a documented framework adapter, or restart/use a compatible enhanced runtime when original-class visibility is required. Understand reflective visibility → Properties changed on disk but runtime values stayed old Inspect rejection/uncheckable output, source ownership, higher-priority values and admission holds. Fix the invalid candidate and save again. Do not assume a startup-only consumer recreates itself. Inspect the configuration path → A listener stopped and the replacement did not start Check retirement timeout and registration/expression errors. A failed addition can leave no new consumer, with old ownership retained or retired depending on the stage. Correct the input and follow the direct-path retry diagnostic. Do not infer successful delivery from class reload. Inspect consumer lifecycle limits → A generated model has a field, but persistence cannot use it Check type-system/schema preparation, native reflective visibility and the mapping path separately. Code generation alone does not install a database column. Inspect the persistence layers → Reload waits while requests keep running Request mode reopens traffic after its drain deadline and queues the edit for a natural idle boundary. Check unfinished async work and Callable workers, especially when cancellation is ignored. Inspect request-boundary behavior →

title: Recover deliberately
text: Recover deliberately For a bad implementation, restore the previous source and compile again. Recheck the same application behavior. If a lifecycle/registration/schema step failed, use the diagnostic’s specific recovery or restart requirement; source reversal does not undo its side effects. For an instrumentation issue, the source supports excludeClasses for a named class or structuralReload=false for method-body-only operation. These are startup configuration changes. Removing the agent flag runs without the agent after restart. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Report a reproducible issue
text: Report a reproducible issue Include the agent/integration versions, Java vendor/version, OS, framework versions, launch route, watched output, minimal before/after edit, compile command, expected/observed result and relevant DIAGNOSE/PENDING output. State whether the same edit works after a fresh restart. Use synthetic names and remove credentials, customer identities, private paths and application data from logs or fixtures. The protocol can expose class names and local output paths. For vulnerability reports follow the project’s security policy. Report an issue ↗ Security policy ↗ Local socket scope ↗

title: How to read a support claim
text: How to read a support claim Support labels are scoped outcomes Label Meaning How to use it Reloads The documented path supports the change within its stated shape. Read the conditions, then check your application result. Conditional An opt-in, special JVM, restricted adapter or follow-up action is needed. Meet the prerequisites before treating it as supported. Restart The described change cannot be completed by this reload path. Perform the named restart/schema/platform action. Unverified The current source registry lacks the required acceptance lane. Run a relevant acceptance test; do not assume success or failure. No reload The source intentionally applies no Reclazz change for this case. A green characterization test for a refusal is not evidence that the feature reloads. Consult the original record for the exact verdict. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Named framework lanes are not a universal matrix
text: Named framework lanes are not a universal matrix Stock SapMachine 17/21 on macOS arm64 are the main recorded lanes. The source targets Java 17+, but other JVM vendors, operating systems, future JDKs and enhanced VMs need their own acceptance evidence. Framework support is feature-specific: Core and ordinary Spring records name their own loader/shape limits. Modern MVC callbacks and native request boundaries have explicit Spring 6.1.14 records. Messaging uses exact Kafka/JMS/Rabbit and broker combinations, listed in its guide. Current native Boot properties/YAML P5 evidence uses Boot 2.7.18, not a fresh complete Boot 3 matrix. File-template observers do not establish packaged-resource or full view integration. SDK-derived Spring graphs are not deployed SAP tenant or cluster acceptance. Read the technical reference ↗

title: Development trust boundary
text: Development trust boundary Writing watched class output can execute code in the application JVM. Opt-in ImpEx/schema features can change the development database. Treat watch directories as trusted application inputs. The local socket binds to 127.0.0.1 and may expose class names and paths to other users who can reach it on the host. This documentation adds no analytics or remote search. Search runs in your browser against the site’s static index. External project links and the site’s existing font host are separate network requests. Read the technical reference ↗ Development trust context ↗

title: Technical reference library

title: Reproducible agentic workflow evaluation
text: This is a fixed, deterministic evaluation of the Reclazz tool workflow. It uses actual compiled class files, the packaged MCP server, the official MCP SDK and a persistent application JVM. It does not measure an LLM, certify an AI desktop client or estimate success rates on arbitrary user tasks. No model API, account or extra dependency is required. Run From the repository root, set JAVA_HOME to the JDK you want to measure, then: sh ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar :mcp-server:mcpRelease npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client test Use gradlew.bat on Windows. Node 22 and a complete JDK with javac are required. The private test project pins SDK 1.30.0. npm test runs the evaluation recorder's negative tests first, then the live acceptance fixture, sequentially. To run only the recorder tests, use npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client run test:evaluation . The existing Linux/Windows JDK17 client CI steps also run and upload this report; a configured lane is not evidence that a particular revision passed there. title: Run
text: Run From the repository root, set JAVA_HOME to the JDK you want to measure, then: sh ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar :mcp-server:mcpRelease npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client test Use gradlew.bat on Windows. Node 22 and a complete JDK with javac are required. The private test project pins SDK 1.30.0. npm test runs the evaluation recorder's negative tests first, then the live acceptance fixture, sequentially. To run only the recorder tests, use npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client run test:evaluation . The existing Linux/Windows JDK17 client CI steps also run and upload this report; a configured lane is not evidence that a particular revision passed there. Each run creates a fresh mcp-server/build/client-matrix/<platform>-<random>/ directory. It retains compiler/application logs and writes evaluation.json with scenario measurements. Ordinary setup/assertion failures also produce a non-passing report after the directory and report hook have been created. Failure before that point, process termination, a machine crash or an unwritable disk cannot guarantee a report. A missing report is never success. The existing evidence.json remains the acceptance-only success artifact. Read the current run's exit status and evaluation.json.passed ; do not reuse an older report. Reports include OS/architecture, Node/JDK/SDK/product versions, Java executable paths and SHA-256 digests of the two installed jars (when setup reached that point). Compare runs using the same artifacts and environment.

title: Fixed scenarios
text: Fixed scenarios The seven scenarios run in this order in one JVM; recovery deliberately depends on the failed build. A failed prerequisite aborts the flow and leaves subsequent scenarios not_run , rather than shrinking the denominator. Scenario Required outcome successful-reload Owned build, actual compile, exact v2 receipt and live v2 behavior in the original JVM with retained service state mixed-batch Service applied, App unobserved; batch remains incomplete and non-atomic failed-build-hold Partial v3 output plus real compiler failure remains unapplied through SCAN; competing owner cannot release it recovery Original owner completes a fresh v4 build; exact receipt and live v4 behavior agree stale-receipt The old v3 hash cannot be claimed as applied after v4 unavailable-target Missing port file is an error, never proof of reload; original application stays alive malformed-input Invalid build state is rejected; MCP ping and original application remain responsive

title: What the numbers mean
text: What the numbers mean Success: all assertions in a named scenario passed, no false completion check fired and no observed target identity change occurred. The summary's successRate is passed scenarios divided by all seven planned scenarios. It is coverage of these fixed cases, not a statistical model success estimate. Overall passed / complete requires the final acceptance checks as well. False completion: a checked positive completion claim lacks its required evidence. BUILD, SCAN and DOCTOR cannot prove reload; a failed/stale request or mixed batch cannot count as complete. Positive VERIFY needs the requested class/hash and original session; an additional independent check requires matching live value, PID, startup nonce and advancing service counter. completionChecks retains claims, proof verdicts and supporting observations. falseCompletions counts failed claim checks, not unique tasks. A receipt and its live-behavior check are separate checks. falseCompletionRate divides by checked positive claims, and is null when there were none. Expected negative responses are successful safety outcomes, not false completions. Polls count as calls; the terminal receipt is scored for completion, not every poll. Restarts: observed changes of PID, startup nonce or target session between identity observations. The first launch is excluded; changing several identity fields together counts once. The fixture never intentionally restarts the JVM. Live probes use the initial DOCTOR session; subsequent receipts are checked against it separately. Missing probes fail the scenario: zero observed restarts on an incomplete run does not establish continuity. The recorded observation count and observations delimit what was actually seen. Calls: SDK tools/call attempts, including verification polling, expected errors and calls that throw. Per-scenario counts and callsByTool are separate from discovery/setup calls; the summary includes both. Initialize, ping, listTools, compilation and live application probes are not tool calls. Elapsed time: monotonic milliseconds per scenario, including its compilation, polling and deliberate hold-observation window. Total time starts after the evidence directory is created and includes setup and final acceptance work, excluding teardown and report writing. These are observations, not latency guarantees; there is no speed ranking or performance threshold. Existing bounded timeouts still fail a stalled test. Recorder tests prove that wrong hashes, sessions, class names, live values, identity and lost state cannot establish completion; falsely claiming success fails a scenario. They also check rejected-call accounting, elapsed intervals, restart counting and preservation of failed/unrun scenarios. They do not replace the actual JVM run. Existing acceptance assertions are retained. This evaluation reuses the client acceptance fixture rather than adding a second build harness. Native Gradle/Maven two-module coverage, framework coverage and interactive client coverage retain the separate limits documented there. This task adds no production protocol or reload behavior.

title: Agentic client acceptance matrix
text: This matrix separates an independent MCP client from Reclazz's own protocol fixtures, and separates an executable CI lane from a lane actually observed passing. SDK acceptance does not certify any desktop AI application or GUI. Independent client mcp-server/src/test/client is a private, test-only npm project. It pins the official MCP TypeScript SDK to 1.30.0 with a lockfile. Node 22 runs the consumer; the installed product still requires only Java. No npm dependency is added to the agent, IDE plugin, build plugins or MCP distribution. The SDK performs initialization/negotiation, ping, tool discovery and calls against the packaged MCP jar over stdio . The test installs both jars under paths containing spaces and launches a real application JVM with the agent. It covers: MCP startup from an unrelated client directory with explicit project and relative port-file defaults; all tools check same-connection target-directory evidence. All nine tools and their advertised output schemas, including error results; JSON text must match structured output. Missing required result fields are rejected by the SDK's own schema validator. DOCTOR target PID, working directory, session and capabilities.

title: Independent client
text: Independent client mcp-server/src/test/client is a private, test-only npm project. It pins the official MCP TypeScript SDK to 1.30.0 with a lockfile. Node 22 runs the consumer; the installed product still requires only Java. No npm dependency is added to the agent, IDE plugin, build plugins or MCP distribution. The SDK performs initialization/negotiation, ping, tool discovery and calls against the packaged MCP jar over stdio . The test installs both jars under paths containing spaces and launches a real application JVM with the agent. It covers: MCP startup from an unrelated client directory with explicit project and relative port-file defaults; all tools check same-connection target-directory evidence. All nine tools and their advertised output schemas, including error results; JSON text must match structured output. Missing required result fields are rejected by the SDK's own schema validator. DOCTOR target PID, working directory, session and capabilities. Observation does not claim that any reload has completed. An acknowledged owned BUILD, actual javac compilation, exact-byte VERIFY and changed behavior in the same application PID and existing service instance. A partial compiler output followed by a real compiler error. Failed output stays unapplied even after SCAN, a competing owner is refused, and the same owner can recover with a complete successful build. Manual pause holds compiled output through SCAN; correlated status shows pending files and resume leads to exact-byte VERIFY and changed behavior in the same JVM. Mixed applied/unobserved batch results, stale hashes, missing target, malformed tool arguments, and continued ping after errors. Neither a BUILD acknowledgement nor a scan is treated as reload completion. Reclazz's Java AgenticEndToEndTest separately covers explicit MCP protocol versions 2024-11-05 and 2025-06-18 . The independent SDK uses its normal negotiation, without overriding or recreating the client's handshake. From the repository root, with JAVA_HOME set to the JDK being tested: sh ./gradlew :agent:shadowJar :mcp-server:mcpRelease npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund npm --prefix mcp-server/src/test/client test On Windows use gradlew.bat for the first command and set JAVA_HOME to a native JDK installation. The test uses absolute java.exe and javac.exe paths with argument arrays, not a shell command assembled from project paths. The Gradle toolchain can differ from JAVA_HOME ; the latter determines the application and MCP processes in this independent test. Each run writes a fresh directory under mcp-server/build/client-matrix/ . evidence.json is written only after all assertions pass, recording SDK/Node/JDK versions, OS/architecture, JVM identity, session and actual tool results. Compiler and application logs remain on failure as well. Do not infer success from a directory's presence or from evidence left by a previous run. The same run also writes evaluation.json with seven named scenario outcomes, false-completion checks, observed restarts, tool-call counts and elapsed time, including failed and unrun scenarios. See workflow evaluation for exact metric definitions and failure-reporting limits. This is a deterministic workflow evaluation, not a model benchmark.

title: Real build tools
text: Real build tools scripts/test-build-plugin-safety.py is the existing separate acceptance harness for actual Gradle and Maven two-module builds . It exercises seven scenarios per tool: ordinary opt-out, partial compilation failure, competing owner, same-owner recovery, exact-byte receipts, up-to-date barrier and offline target refusal before output changes. It talks directly to the agent's socket; it is not another independent MCP SDK client. Build :gradle-plugin:jar , :agent:shadowJar , :mcp-server:shadowJar and package maven-plugin/pom.xml first. The Maven plugin needs the matching agent artifact available in its build repository. The fixture itself overlays artifacts into an isolated repository and does not publish to the user's repository. Existing Gradle and Maven guides describe the opt-in wrappers. sh python3 scripts/test-build-plugin-safety.py --help python3 scripts/test-build-plugin-safety.py \ --work-dir /tmp/reclazz-client-build-acceptance \ --gradle /absolute/path/to/gradle-8.10.2/bin/gradle Use a fresh work directory every time. The default artifacts are for 1.5.0; for another version pass --version and the matching artifact paths shown by --help . Maven 3.9.x and its fixture compiler plugin must be cached for this offline harness. The cache-overlay script uses symlinks; Windows execution of this separate harness is not claimed by the SDK CI lane.

title: Execution status
text: Execution status The current change adds the SDK test to existing Ubuntu/JDK17 and Windows/JDK17 CI lanes using Node22. Both upload consumer evidence. These are configured lanes; a passing hosted run must be checked for the relevant commit. The existing Ubuntu/JDK21 lane keeps the Java protocol tests. Observed locally on 2026-09-23 , macOS aarch64, Node22.20.0: Consumer / runtime Observed result Scope Official SDK 1.30.0 / SAP JDK 17.0.16 PASS Eight tools, 18 invalid output mutations rejected, live reload/failure/recovery Official SDK 1.30.0 / SAP JDK 21.0.10.0.1 PASS Same acceptance against a separately launched JDK21 application and MCP process Gradle 8.10.2 / SAP JDK21 PASS Seven real two-module build scenarios using the existing fixture Maven 3.9.16 / SAP JDK21 PASS Seven real two-module build scenarios using the existing fixture SDK / Windows JDK17 Not run locally CI configured; no hosted result claimed here SDK / Linux JDK17 Not run locally CI configured; no hosted result claimed here Native build fixture / Windows Not run SDK acceptance does not imply native Gradle/Maven fixture acceptance Inspector GUI / desktop AI clients Not run No GUI or account acceptance claim The negative witness bypassed the failed build's hold in a temporary test copy. The same application probe failed with live value 3 where held value 2 was required. The committed test always uses the hold; no production source was modified for this experiment. Inspector GUI, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other interactive clients are not certified by these tests. No external account or hosted service is needed for the local acceptance flow. On 2026-10-03 , the pause/resume extension passed locally on macOS aarch64, Node22.20.0, official SDK1.30.0 and SAP JDK17.0.16: nine tools, 23 invalid output mutations rejected, paused output retained through SCAN, then exact-byte verification and changed behavior after resume in the same JVM/instance. This additional run does not establish hosted CI or JDK21 acceptance for the new control tool. On 2026-10-03 , explicit-project startup also passed the local macOS aarch64 SDK1.30.0 / Node22.20.0 / SAP JDK17.0.16 acceptance: MCP ran from the jar install directory while the app ran from the selected consumer project. All nine tools worked with startup defaults; seven evaluation scenarios passed with zero false completions or restarts. Hosted and Windows runs for this extension remain unrun.

title: Build and preview
text: Build and preview Use Python 3.9+ in an isolated environment. The pinned dependencies are documentation build tools only; they do not enter the agent, IDE plugin or Maven/Gradle artifacts. sh python3 -m venv .venv-docs .venv-docs/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt .venv-docs/bin/python scripts/build-docs-site.py .venv-docs/bin/python scripts/check-docs-site.py .venv-docs/bin/python scripts/test-docs-site.py python3 -m http.server 18765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory build/site On Windows use .venv-docs/Scripts/python.exe instead of .venv-docs/bin/python . Open http://127.0.0.1:18765/docs/ . Check a complete reference page, its internal links, tables and code examples; also check desktop/mobile, both themes, search and keyboard navigation. Build output is ignored and must not be edited by hand. sh .venv-docs/bin/python scripts/build-docs-site.py --check This check rejects stale output when a source, option, asset or build input changed. The build manifest records every canonical document’s digest and public route. The reference library includes JSON evidence downloads; it does not certify that those acceptance runs were repeated by a documentation build.

title: Continuous integration and publication
text: Continuous integration and publication The docs workflow builds and checks documentation-only changes separately from the application test gate. Pull requests produce a site artifact for review and never deploy. A successful main push can deploy the same checked artifact through GitHub Pages Actions. Its GitHub environment and repository branch protections remain the owner’s controls; this task does not change those settings. Before the first production deployment, finish independent review/commit and set Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions . The previous branch-based site and custom domain stay in service until that switch and a successful deployment. Do not delete a live branch as part of local migration. The workflow retains CNAME , .nojekyll and all existing landing/privacy/license assets in the built site. No separate branch synchronization or copying of docs is needed after adoption. Do not use a generated gh-pages file as source.

title: Version and evidence discipline
text: Version and evidence discipline Keep capability evidence tied to its recorded source/version. Site generation must not upgrade an unverified lane or a component-only test into a watcher acceptance claim. Source presence does not prove artifact publication. If a claim moves out of README, relocate its registry surface path/line/quote and file digest; keep verdicts, observing tests and execution records unchanged. Run the existing evidence, protocol and argument checks before handoff. Full reference pages rewrite known Markdown links to site routes. Links to source code, examples or non-rendered project files retain the source repository location. Markdown HTML/XML examples belong in code fences. Literal angle-bracket prose is escaped; existing empty ID anchors remain linkable. Curated layout fragments under docs/site/ retain their separate HTML authoring path. Keep examples synthetic and remove private names, credentials and customer paths.

title: One source per fact
text: One source per fact Installation actions and runnable setup snippets: docs/installation.md and docs/maven.md . Quickstart uses {{INCLUDE docs/file.md#heading}} to render the canonical section; do not paste its commands into an HTML fragment. Missing sections fail the build. Agent arguments/defaults: docs/usage.md . The product reference links here and the options page is generated from this table. Support outcomes/conditions/actions: docs/reload-support.md . Keep linked technical scope precise; these are bounded editorial summaries, not automatic certification of the runtime test registries. Do not independently author a support JSON file. Source version: pluginVersion in gradle.properties . Evidence commit and actual review date: docs/site/manifest.json . Reviewing docs does not rerun acceptance tests. The build revision is separately recorded; never silently advance recorded evidence. AI discovery: llms.txt is generated from the README introduction and page metadata; no independent feature claims or support matrix are authored there. Use {{REF docs/usage.md#heading}} for guide reading links. These resolve to website references; source-code links retain the selected build revision. The evidence footer retains the explicit capability baseline. Fix relative Markdown links at their source so GitHub/offline reading also works; website aliases are not a source-link repair. The checker validates source anchors as well as rendered routes, evidence surface hashes, and the absence of independently editable AI/support outputs. Search links directly to sections. The large evidence registry remains available in full, but only its introduction is indexed to avoid making every reader download thousands of provenance lines. Maintainer publishing/workflow pages have their own navigation group. Full reference URLs and heading anchors remain stable when navigation is reorganized. When changing a heading, preserve a legacy empty ID anchor or update every canonical link to it.

title: Shared public layout
text: Shared public layout website/layout.py owns the public header, footer, search dialog and shared head assets for documentation, home, comparison, privacy and license pages. Public HTML under website/static/ keeps its content and metadata, using the SITE_HEAD , SITE_HEADER , SITE_FOOTER and SITE_UTILITIES markers exactly once. The builder rejects bypasses. Shared visual tokens remain in website/static/docs/assets/docs.css ; assets/site.css styles the public navigation/footer and assets/marketing.css styles public content. assets/site.js enhances the native mobile navigation; assets/home.js owns the existing homepage FAQ and English/Turkish copy. Theme and docs search are shared across every page. The full license uses native details so it works with a keyboard and without JavaScript. The site checker validates all public HTML pages, their assets and local anchors in addition to the documentation contracts. After layout changes, check mobile navigation, search, theme persistence between pages, language switching and horizontal table scrolling.

title: Core JVM feature evidence
text: This is the first checkpoint of the all-advertised-features evidence program. It classifies the listed core promises; it does not certify every feature, framework, program, JDK or operating system. Other evidence packages remain separate. Records distinguish PROVEN_WITH_SCOPE (observed watcher behavior on both named lanes), PARTIAL (component observations only), EXPECTED (observed limitation/refusal), FAILED (a capability fails despite a passing characterization test) and UNVERIFIED (missing run/environment). Independent Claude review is pending until the package audit is archived. The available lanes are stock SapMachine17/21 on macOS arm64. Other provider/OS/enhanced cells remain unverified. Deferred field-initializer concurrency stays deferred. Raw logs/XML are retained locally at the paths in the JSON; the JSON contains method results and provenance, not a substitute claim that every green receipt establishes behavior. Reproduce with the repository tasks :agent:unitTest --rerun and :agent:e2eTest --rerun on each named runtime, then check P1RegistryCompletenessTest . The check rejects omitted cells, stale public surfaces, nonexistent test methods, component-as-watcher promotion

title: For AI agents
text: This page is for a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Aider and the like) working on a Spring Boot or SAP Commerce project. It tells you how to run that project with Reclazz so your code edits take effect in the running JVM without a restart, and how to confirm that they did. What Reclazz gives your edit-run loop Reclazz is a -javaagent that watches compiled class files and hot-swaps them into the running JVM in place. State is preserved, so the app keeps running across your edits. It is free, open source, sends no telemetry, and needs no IDE: everything below is a shell command or a build-file edit, the two things an agent already does. Turn it on Pick the build you are in. Each path attaches the agent to the dev run and the test JVM, so a plain bootRun / mvn test runs against reloaded classes. Gradle (plugin) kotlin plugins { id("org.springframework.boot") version "3.3.0" id("com.onurkat.reclazz") version "1.5.0" } The plugin resolves com.onurkat.reclazz:reclazz-agent from Maven Central and wires the flag into bootRun and Test . It is published on the Gradle Plugin Portal, so the id(...) version "1.5.0" form above resolves as-is. Details and options: gradle-plu
